title: Who owns American time and savings deposits, by kind of owner

rows.name: Households and nonprofit organizations
rows.basis: what is left over after every measured owner

rows.name: State and local government employee defined benefit pension funds

source: Federal Reserve Board, Financial Accounts of the United States (Z.1), table F2_3_s (amounts outstanding) and F2_3_t_tu (transactions, not seasonally adjusted), one line per holding sector
note: The share of each owner is of everything outstanding. Net bought is the Federal Reserve's quarterly net purchases; price and other changes is the change in holdings minus what was bought, which is mostly price moves. The Fed carries Treasury, agency, municipal and corporate bond totals at face value and most holders at market value, which is part of its published gap. Time and savings deposits are money left with banks and credit unions for a return, such as savings accounts and certificates of deposit; what is owed is the banks' and credit unions' published liability. Households here are what is left after every measured holder, as the Fed computes them. This book is money, so it is not added into the world ledger's total of owned wealth.
